newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends higher amid steady cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends higher amid steady cash.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended mostly higher Thursday after some late buying pushed May out of its recent narrow range, industry sources said.

May finished 3.8 cents higher at $1.905 after hitting a high of $1.925. June, which reached a high of $1.975, settled up 3.9 cents at $1.966. Other deferreds were up by a narrower margin, thereby weakening spreads to the summer months.
"The forecast for below-normal temperatures for next week may be lending some support, and there may also be enough storage buying interest to hold prices for the moment," one source said.

Technically, support in May was still pegged at $1.825, $1.78 and the contract low of $1.71. Beyond those levels traders said next support was at $1.65-1.70. Resistance was seen at $1.95-1.97 and $2.04-2.05.
NYMEX's 12-month strip rose 2.2 cents to $2.104 as an estimated 26,828 Hub contracts traded. Open interest for April 2 lost 406 lots to 165,925.

In the cash market, U.S. Gulf Coast prices were slightly softer on Transco (Station 65) in the high-$1.80s, while Henry Hub prices were about one cent higher at $1.86-1.88. Prices on the Midcontinent pipes were mostly steady at $1.72-1.75, with Chicago city-gate quoted around $1.90. At the New York city-gate, gas prices eased to about $2.15.

Temperatures throughout the U.S. are expected to remain normal to above normal through the weekend, except in the Southwest where temperatures are forecast to hover several degrees below normal, Weather Services Corp.
In its six- to 10-day forecast, below-normal temperatures are expected to blanket about two-thirds of the U.S., excluding the Southwest, where normal to above-normal temperatures will likely return.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded.
On KCBT, May settled three cents higher at $1.76, while deferreds were mostly two cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.8 cent to 14.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
Physical prices in the Permian basin remained even with futures in the low-to-mid $1.70s.
